subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback when explicit bindings miss, or should explicit account bindings remain the only supported routing contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but changing fallback behavior can cross session, model/provider, tool, and permission boundaries for existing multi-account setups.

options.title: Approve guarded fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep explicit bindings only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and add clearer doctor/status/docs guidance for Discord accounts that look intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Repair the fork PR first
options.body: Use the open fork PR as source material only after resolving conflicts, adding the missing safety guards, and supplying real Discord proof.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the multi-agent routing contract and Discord channel routing boundary where steipete has the strongest feature-history signal.
